tools.name: set_copper_zones
tools.description: Replace a saved PCB layout's complete custom copper-pour set without changing its poses, traces, vias, outline, or text. Each zone is a conductive filled polygon on a routable signal layer (including plane-free inner layers such as In3.Cu); its net and layer are validated against the design, and invalid/self-intersecting polygons reject the whole call. Pass zones:[] to clear custom pours. Returns {ok,live_version,layout,zones,routed,total,drc,drc_errors,open[]}; connectivity and DRC include the new pours.

name.description: Design name or a lib/modules module name.

layout.description: Target a named saved layout instead of the working/starred one.

zones.description: The complete replacement set of conductive copper zones.

net.description: Net name exactly as describe_pcb_layout reports it.

layer.description: Routable copper layer name, e.g. F.Cu, B.Cu, or a plane-free inner layer such as In3.Cu.

poly.description: Simple polygon as at least three [x,y] board-mm vertices.

priority.description: KiCad-style fill priority; a higher different-net zone wins an overlap.

group.description: Optional stamped-subcircuit ownership tag to preserve when replacing grouped zones.

tools.name: list_designs
tools.description: List designs available in this project (one per .sexp file in src/ containing a top-level design-block). Returns an array of objects with fields: name (file basename), title (human-readable design-block title), sections (array of top-level section names), instance_count, net_count, mtime (Unix seconds of last source modification), build_ok (false if the design failed to evaluate, in which case counts and sections are empty).

tools.name: list_library
tools.description: List names available in the project's lib/ (components, modules, pinouts, footprints). Without a query the response is lean: each category is {count,names[...]} — names only, no descriptions, sorted alphabetically (no per-file reads, so it is fast even on a large library). With a query each category becomes a ranked [{name,description}] array. Matching covers names and descriptions; module descriptions additionally index the defmodule doc string and explicit (implements component (policy ...) (role ...)) metadata, so searching for an MPN/component or role discovers reusable implementations. Results are capped at `limit` (default 50) per category. Optional `category` scopes either mode to a single subdir. Use the returned names in (import ...) forms and prefer canonical/recommended modules reported by describe_component.

query.description: Optional fuzzy filter over each entry's name + description, including module docs and implementation metadata. Omit or leave blank for the lean names-only listing.

category.description: Optional: scope the response to a single library subdir.

limit.description: Max ranked entries per category when a query is given (default 50). Ignored without a query.

tools.name: list_history
tools.description: List snapshot ids for a design, newest first. Each id is a timestamp usable with restore_version.

tools.name: list_instances
tools.description: List every instance in the design. By default (flatten=true) this walks the whole design tree: each entry has ref_des (sub-block-prefixed, e.g. ldo/U2), origin (the module-local source name, e.g. U1, or null at top level), component family, symbol, value, and pin_count (from the part's pinout, so a connector with no symbol still counts its pads). Pass flatten=false for the top-level-only view (ref_des, label, component, symbol, value, pin_count). Use this to bridge source-side names (stm32, expansion) and board-side ref_des. `name` accepts a design or a lib/modules module name — modules resolve standalone via their parameter defaults (real instantiations are not consulted).

variant.description: Assembly variant to evaluate the design in, from the design's (variant "NAME") declarations. Omit for its (default) variant, else the base. A design that declares variants also returns a variants[] catalog, the selected variant, and per-instance populated_in.

flatten.description: Flatten sub-blocks into the whole design tree (default true). Pass false for the top-level-only view.

tools.name: list_free_pins
tools.description: List unassigned pins on an instance with their default pinout function names and a best-effort category (gpio|power|clock|analog|other). By default (flatten=true) `ref` matches a flattened instance by exact ref, sub-block leaf, or module-local origin name, and assignments are read from the merged netlist (so a sub-block child's wired pads show their canonical rail names); pass flatten=false for the top-level-only instance. Use for picking GPIOs for new peripherals without scanning the full pinout file.

ref.description: Reference designator of the instance (e.g. U1)

flatten.description: Flatten sub-blocks into the whole design tree (default true). Pass false for the top-level-only view.

tools.name: get_net
tools.description: Return every pin connection on a net plus any passive instances (R/L/C/F/D) on it. By default (flatten=true) the net is resolved against the flattened, net-tie-merged netlist: pass the canonical merged name or a sub-scoped spelling (e.g. ldo/VOUT) and get every pin on the whole merged rail with sub-block-prefixed refs. Pass flatten=false for the top-level-only net. Use to audit decoupling or verify wiring without scanning the whole source. `name` accepts a design or a lib/modules module name — modules resolve standalone via their parameter defaults (real instantiations are not consulted).

flatten.description: Flatten sub-blocks into the whole design tree (default true). Pass false for the top-level-only view.

tools.name: describe_component
tools.description: Describe a library component or component-family by name. Reads lib/components/<name>.sexp, its pinout, and reusable-module metadata in one call. Returns component identity, datasheets, pins, requirements, and implementations[{module,policy,role,description,source_sha256}]. A canonical implementation must be instantiated through its sub-block module unless the direct instance carries (module-bypass "reason"); recommended implementations produce an authoring warning; examples are discovery-only. source_sha256 is the deterministic module revision digest for review/CI dependency-drift checks. pins is the full pad→function map resolved through the evaluator path. check_kind is the same primitive label build-time review uses. Call this before instantiating a part and prefer the reported canonical/recommended implementation. Returns {ok:false,error} if the component is missing.

name.description: Component basename (e.g. "adar2004accz", "cap-0402"). Same names list_library returns under "components".

tools.name: get_schematic
tools.description: Fetch a design's schematic. view=summary (DEFAULT) returns a compact projection - {ok,name,title,ports,instances (ref_des+component+value, no per-pin detail),nets (name+pin_count),sub_blocks,erc,assertions} - the same shape preview_module returns for a module, compact enough for ordinary scripts on real boards. view=scene_graph (alias: full) returns the complete scene-graph JSON the browser viewer renders; it is LARGE, so request it only for a small design or when you genuinely need per-pin geometry. `name` accepts a design or a lib/modules module name - modules resolve standalone via their parameter defaults (real instantiations are not consulted).

view.description: summary (default) = compact netlist + ERC + assertions, compact for routine use; scene_graph (alias full) = the complete scene-graph JSON - request it only when you truly need the full geometry.

tools.name: get_schematic_image
tools.description: Render a schematic block natively as a PNG image for visual review after edits — no browser, DOM, Chromium, or Playwright. Uses the exact SVG layout/display-list path as the schematic page and PDF export. `view=functional` (default) groups connected pins and draws recognised direct returns; `view=sequential` preserves physical pin order and label-connected endpoints. Focus with `sub=<slug>` for one sub-circuit card or `ref=<hub>` for one IC hub; a small module/design with at most eight hubs can render as an unfocused contact sheet. `theme=dark|light` selects the web or print palette. `name` accepts a design or a lib/modules module name.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

sub.description: Slugified sub-block name, matching the schematic card's data-slug.

ref.description: Exact hub ref-des, or a unique path leaf. Use the full path when a leaf is ambiguous.

theme.description: Dark web palette (default) or light print palette.

tools.name: get_pcb_layout_image
tools.description: Render a design's PCB layout (force-directed auto-placement) as a PNG image so you can VISUALLY inspect part arrangement, decoupling loops, airwires, and optionally routed copper — not just parse coordinate JSON. Returns base64 JSON by default, or decoded PNG bytes with --output. A plain call shows the whole board; pass nets and/or refs to enter focus mode: the named nets and components are spotlighted in amber while everything else is dimmed, for studying one subsystem in context. Airwire colours: orange=hot decoupling loop, cyan=ground return, grey=signal. With route=true it also overlays red=top-copper / blue=bottom-copper traces, vias, and red rings on DRC violations. Uses the design's saved auto-layout when present (set regen=true to force a fresh solve). The header always prints the objective breakdown (obj / hpwl / loop nH / compactness / congestion). Diagnostic overlays for figuring out what to improve: blame=true (cost heatmap + worst-offenders, the best starting view), loops=true (per-loop nH labels), dims=true (mm distances cap→pin), grid=true (mm reference grid), and compare=<saved-layout> (diff against another layout with movement arrows + Δobjective). Part labels follow names=ref|origin|both (spec-driven renders default to origin names, the vocabulary the (placement ...) spec uses). pins=["U13"] (or "hubs") labels pad net names on those parts. When a (placement ...) spec drove the solve, the header shows its coverage (SPEC: ALL PLACED / N UNPLACED / FELL BACK TO AUTO) and spec-unlisted parts are pin-hug AUTO-FILLED beside their placed pads (amber outline - usable, but the spec doesn't pin them); a part the solver couldn't safely place is hatched red in a staging band (NOT deliberately placed). Side lists accept (net "VIN") membership rules that expand to every unclaimed part on that net. Extra views: crop= zooms on one part (r= radius mm), cropnet= zooms to a net set's pads + copper (the per-trace lens), sheet=true returns a contact sheet (board + per-hub closeups), critique=true draws a numbered worst-problems overlay. Set thermal=true for the HEAT-ZONE view instead: the same board painted with its steady-state temperature field, with scenario= choosing the cooling assumption.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

nets.description: Net names to spotlight (case-insensitive). Also accepts a comma-separated string.

refs.description: Reference designators to spotlight, e.g. ["U1","C3"]. Also accepts a comma-separated string.

route.description: Route fresh and overlay copper traces, vias, and DRC violations. WITHOUT it (default), the shown layout's persisted copper is restored, DRC-checked against the current poses, and drawn (page parity) — so saved routing is visible without a slow full re-route.

width.description: Output image width in pixels (default 1200; clamped).

layout.description: Render a specific saved layout by name instead of the auto layout.

sub.description: Scope the render to a single sub-block (slugified sub-block name).

regen.description: Force a fresh placement solve instead of using the cached auto-layout.

rough.description: Use the ROUGH seed instead of the force solve: each module is kept as an intact, grid-aligned rigid block (a flat module rings the anchor IC with each passive on the side of the pad it serves). A legible, module-coherent starting point, deliberately not metric-optimal; forces a fresh solve.

blame.description: Blame heatmap: tint each component by its share of the objective (green=cheap, red=expensive) and list the 3 worst-placed parts top-right. Best first view for deciding what to move.

loops.description: Label each decoupling loop with its connection inductance (nH); ribbon width scales with it.

dims.description: Draw labelled mm dimension leaders on each hot loop's power leg (cap-pad-to-IC-pin distance).

grid.description: Overlay a 1/2/5 mm reference grid with axis tick labels for absolute measurement.

compare.description: Saved-layout name to diff the current placement against: ghost outlines + movement arrows + a delta-objective in the score line.

names.description: Part-name labels: 'ref' = flattened ref-des (C150), 'origin' = the stable module-local name a (placement ...) spec is written in (C_BOOT1), 'both' = REF=ORIGIN. Default: origin when a (placement ...) spec drives the solve, ref otherwise.

pins.description: Label these parts' pads with their net names (VIN/SW/FB/GND) so pin functions are readable off the image. Case-insensitive refs (sub-block leaf ok); the token 'hubs' labels every hub IC. Also accepts a comma-separated string.

crop.description: Zoom: crop the viewport to a window around this part (ref-des, sub-block leaf, or origin name). Combine with pins= for a readable pin-level closeup.

cropnet.description: Zoom lens: crop the viewport to these nets' pads + their routed/restored copper + a ~1.5mm margin (net matching like nets=). When both crop= and cropnet= are given, crop= wins. Also accepts a comma-separated string.

sheet.description: Contact sheet: the whole board plus per-hub pin-labeled closeups in one image.

critique.description: Callout overlay: numbered markers + a fix-first panel (hottest loops by nH, longest airwire, staged parts, DRC count).

thermal.description: HEAT-ZONE view: paint the board's steady-state temperature field instead of its copper — the picture twin of describe_thermal. Each part's dissipation and thermal resistances come from the lumped screen (eval/thermal), the field from a 2D spread over the placement's own outline and stackup. Powered parts are labelled with their junction temperature, the hotspot is marked, isotherm lines and a numeric colour bar carry the scale, and the caption names the scenario, the ambient and the highest ambient the board tolerates. Ignores the copper view's own arguments (nets/refs focus, route, crop/cropnet, sheet, critique, compare, blame, loops, dims, grid, pins, names); width/layout/regen/rough/sub still choose and frame the board.

scenario.description: Which cooling scenario the heat field is solved for (thermal=true only; default natural). fan uses the board-authored model, position, face, standoff and installed-flow assumption; the fixed airflow rungs remain comparison brackets; heatsink is the sink-only scenario; fan_heatsink applies the specified fan and passive heatsink together, with fan airflow confined to its selected PCB face. An unrecognised value falls back to still air.

tools.name: describe_pcb_layout
tools.description: Structured spatial facts about a design's solved PCB placement - the textual twin of get_pcb_layout_image, built from the IDENTICAL placement so the facts always describe the board the image shows. Use the two together: the image for gestalt, this for measurements. Returns JSON with: axes convention (y grows down; 'top' = -y, matching (placement ...) spec words); anchor (the largest hub IC facts are oriented around); board w/h mm; score (objective/hpwl/loop_nh); parts[] each with ref + origin (the stable module-local name a (placement ...) spec uses) + kind/x/y/rot/size + side (left|right|top|bottom of the anchor) + gap_mm (courtyard clearance to the anchor) + nets[] on its pads + auto_filled flag (pin-hug placed, spec doesn't pin it) + unplaced flag (solver found no safe spot, still staged); loops[] (each decoupling loop's cap, hub, net, power-leg mm, inductance nH, and which side of the hub the cap sits on); hub_pads[] (per hub IC, each net's package edge(s) and pad count - e.g. VIN pads on the left edge); placement spec coverage (source spec|force, unplaced + auto_filled ref lists); and with route=true a routed summary (trace_mm/tracks/vias/drc). Accepts the same placement-selection args as the image tool.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

route.description: Route fresh and include routed:{trace_mm,tracks,vias,drc}. WITHOUT it, any persisted copper on the shown layout is restored, DRC-checked, and reported the same way (page parity).

layout.description: Describe a specific saved layout by name instead of the auto layout.

sub.description: Scope to a single sub-block (slugified sub-block name).

regen.description: Force a fresh placement solve instead of the cached auto-layout.

rough.description: Describe the ROUGH seed instead of the force solve: each module kept as an intact, grid-aligned rigid block (a flat module rings the anchor IC with each passive on the side of the pad it serves). Deliberately not metric-optimal; forces a fresh solve.

cropnet.description: Zoom-lens net set: emit crop_bbox — the world bbox of these nets' pads + copper + a ~1.5mm margin (net matching like the image tool's nets=), the numeric twin of the PNG viewport. Also accepts a comma-separated string.

pads.description: Add the full pad table (every pad's ref/pad/net/x/y/hw/hh/side/thru) - the OBSTACLE SET. Off by default because it roughly doubles the payload on a dense board; turn it on when you are about to lay copper with add_tracks and must dodge the pads a straight bridge would cut through.

tools.name: get_layout_progress
tools.description: The PCB completion-progress ladder for a design or module's blessed (starred) or named layout - the read-only twin of describe_pcb_layout, returning the same progress block that endpoint embeds. Six ordered rungs, each with a done/total tally and the still-open work: schematic (no ERC errors), sub_circuits (every needs-layout sub-block has a starred module layout), board_setup (a board outline exists), placement (every part locked), routing (every routable net connected by persisted copper), fab_ready (the fab-readiness gate passes on a saved layout). Returns JSON {name, current (the first not-done rung), current_wave? / warnings? (when a (pcb-plan ...) form splits the placement/routing rungs into ordered waves), stages[] each with {id,status,done,total,waves?,items[]}}. Run it to see how done a board is and what the next concrete step is.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

layout.description: Score a specific saved layout by name instead of the blessed (starred) one.

sub.description: Scope to a single sub-block (slugified sub-block name).

regen.description: Score a fresh placement solve instead of the cached auto-layout. A fresh solve carries no persisted copper, so the routing and fab_ready rungs read empty - use it to score a re-solve's placement, not board completion.

rough.description: Score the ROUGH seed instead of the blessed (starred) layout: each module kept as an intact, grid-aligned rigid block (a flat module rings the anchor IC with each passive on the side of the pad it serves). Forces a fresh solve, so - like regen - no saved copper is credited.

tools.name: review_audit
tools.description: Render a board's Release Review Audit as Markdown from generated evidence: identity and release token, the release-profile check summary (ERC, requirements, datasheet reviews, component-class profile gaps, evaluator warnings), the per-component profile table, the layout completion ladder, the fab-readiness gate with its DRC counts by kind, open design notes, and a findings register. Disposition cells are left for the reviewer. The same document `netlisp review-audit <board>` writes; it parses under the system-review Markdown rules, so it can be registered as a board-scoped review document. Read-only.

name.description: Design name

layout.description: Saved layout row to audit (default: the starred layout)

tools.name: review_checklist
tools.description: Generate the board's scoped 258-item engineering review as structured JSON. Purchase sourcing and fabrication-output paperwork are excluded; configured DRC remains the fabrication-rule authority. The response includes exact fitted-MPN datasheet coverage and a mandatory agent contract: do not record needs_info while BOM, library, datasheet, schematic, layout, or built-in analysis tools can obtain the evidence. Agents must fetch/upload missing PDFs, read them, calculate at the board operating point, then record the result.

name.description: Design name

layout.description: Saved layout row to assess (default: the starred layout)

tools.name: review_datasheet_inventory
tools.description: Inventory datasheet evidence for every unique exact fitted MPN in a board's generated BOM. Reports local, remote_only, missing, or missing_mpn plus all affected ref-des and the mandatory next action. Agents must read local PDFs; fetch remote URLs; and call download_datasheet, falling back to manufacturer search plus fetch_datasheet, for missing PDFs before declaring needs_info.

name.description: Design name whose generated BOM supplies exact fitted MPNs

tools.name: record_review_item
tools.description: Record one evidence-backed AI-agent disposition in the generated review sidecar. Before needs_info, agents must exhaust retrievable BOM/library/datasheet/schematic/layout evidence. needs_info requires attempted naming tools, exact MPNs, and outcomes; a datasheet-related blocker is rejected unless read_datasheet plus download_datasheet, fetch_datasheet, or an identified local PDF was attempted. pass/fail/na still require evidence or a note; open restores the generated verdict.

name.description: Design name

id.description: Stable checklist id from review_checklist, e.g. 4.5.10

evidence.description: Concrete refdes/net/layer/report/datasheet section and page evidence

note.description: Agent interpretation or the exact external evidence still missing

attempted.description: Required for needs_info: tools, exact MPNs/inputs, and concrete retrieval or analysis outcomes

agent.description: Agent/model identity stamped on the disposition

tools.name: compare_layout_to_starred
tools.description: Score a design ?rough=1 auto-seed against its STARRED layout (the saved layout marked default/star in /pcb-layout - the hand-finished reference). Interchangeable-aware: each rough part is matched to the nearest starred part of the same class (kind + value + footprint + net set), so swapping which fungible 100nF cap sits on an edge is not penalized. Returns JSON {name, starred, n, area_match_pct (fraction of parts in the same general area - per interchangeable class, per IC edge, count agreement - the right-area headline; tolerant of looseness, only the wrong edge/proportion costs), classes[] each {class, n, matched, rough{per-edge counts}, starred{per-edge counts}} showing which subsystem the rough scattered onto different edges than the hand}. starred is null with a message when nothing is starred yet. Measures how hand-like the rough seed is / how little dragging remains to finish by hand, NOT the electrical score.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

tools.name: routability_preflight
tools.description: STATIC routability preflight - geometrically doomed routing situations read off the PLACEMENT and the design rules alone. Runs NO router: no raster, no net search, no solve. Every finding is a closed-form comparison between a measured millimetre gap and the millimetres that net class's copper demands, so a verdict does not move when routing order, (net-class (priority ...)) or effort tier change - which is exactly why it is worth asking BEFORE spending a solve on remedies that cannot work. Five gates: pad-corridor-tight (sibling pads whose lane cannot admit the class width), via-in-pad-conflict (adjacent SMD pads whose centres cannot both carry their class vias; reserve one transition and surface-fan the other), pad-sealed (all eight octilinear exits blocked), escape-contended (a hub fan has fewer jointly-assignable lanes than nets), and port-blocked (a module port cannot reach outside its block). Corridor capacity in general is deliberately not guessed. Returns {name, routed:false, findings[] each with rule, severity, refs[], msg, a/b, have_mm, need_mm, width_mm, clearance_mm, exits_blocked, counts:{total,corridor,via_in_pad,sealed,escape,port_blocked}}. Identical geometry across many parts collapses into one bucketed finding. The same findings also appear in describe_pcb_layout's lint[] as prose.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

layout.description: Check a specific saved layout by name instead of the blessed (starred) one.

sub.description: Scope to a single sub-block (slugified sub-block name).

regen.description: Check a fresh placement solve instead of the cached auto-layout.

rough.description: Check the ROUGH seed instead of the blessed (starred) layout: each module kept as an intact, grid-aligned rigid block (a flat module rings the anchor IC with each passive on the side of the pad it serves). Forces a fresh solve, and the gates then measure that seed's geometry.

tools.name: route_experiment
tools.description: Route a design's blessed (★ else auto) PCB placement REQUEST-LOCALLY and score it - the read-only, NEVER-PERSISTS twin of route_pcb, for the constraint-DSL routing loop (edit routing plan → route → read score + open nets → iterate). Unlike route_pcb it writes nothing: no sidecar, no .layouts.json, no route cache. The optional plan arg is a complete (pcb-plan …) s-expression fragment that REPLACES the design's authored plan for THIS run only (parsed by the real evaluator, lowered through the same seam route_pcb uses); an unknown wave/class/net name comes back as a plan_warnings entry, and a malformed fragment returns a structured parse-position error. The shown layout's hand-drawn pours ride along as connecting copper, so this measures the same board describe_pcb_layout reports. Returns JSON {name, layout (the saved layout routed, null = the starred one), effort (the retry tier used), plan_source ('override'|'design'), plan_warnings[] each {kind,wave,name,message}, routed, total, vias, trace_mm, drc_errors, score (the deterministic route_score, higher is better), score_v (its formula version), topology (present ONLY when the global topology planner ran: {waves_planned, guides_emitted, nets_skipped_low_confidence}), stuck[] (per unrouted net: failure_mode, blockers, ranked dsl/code remedies - identical shape to describe_pcb_layout's routed.stuck), unrouted[] (the CONNECTIVITY ORACLE's still-open net names - trust these over stuck[], which is router-derived, capped, and can be empty while routed<total), open_nets[] (per open net {net, islands, pads, gaps[] each {mm, from/to {ref,pad,x,y,side}}) - the pad-to-pad hops that would close it, which is what you aim add_tracks at; omitted when nothing is open)}. With repair_placement:true the result also carries placement_repair {verdict, pinches[] each {channel,a,b,need_mm,have_mm,x,y,layer}, moves[] each {ref,opens,x,y,from_x,from_y,dist_mm}, refused[] each {ref,channel,why}, and trial {routed,total,drc_errors,kept} when a trial ran} - the engine-computed placement repair, which writes nothing to disk. Uses the same local module seeding, saved-module fallback, waypoint seeding, global route and perimeter copper as route_pcb; DRC includes shown pours. Diagnostics inspect the final copper after routing. subcircuit_seeds reports the actual local pass. The scalar score is for display, not an adoption policy.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

plan.description: Optional complete (pcb-plan …) fragment that replaces the design's authored routing plan for this run only, e.g. (pcb-plan (route (wave "exp" (rest) (allowed-layers "F.Cu" "B.Cu")))).

layout.description: Saved layout to route against (default: the starred ★ snapshot, else the auto cache). Echoed back in the result so a recorded trial names the board it measured.

sub.description: Scope to a single sub-block (slugified sub-block name).

effort.description: Router retry tier for this run, overriding the design's (route (effort …)). one_shot: one deterministic pass - a net the maze cannot route fails immediately with its diagnosis instead of entering the escalate/rip-up/rescue ladder, which is the mode for an agent iterating on the plan. standard: the historical unattended behaviour. Absent keeps whatever the design declares.

topology.description: Optional: force the global topology planner onto EVERY route wave of the plan for this run only, as if each wave had authored (topology). Plans a whole-wave corridor topology before the maze runs, emitted as soft router guides. Needs a plan (the override above, or the design's own) - with neither there are no route waves to flag.

repair_placement.description: Optional: after the baseline route, probe every declared diff pair's envelope and each still-open net's shortest closing hop for the PLACEMENT geometry walling it, compute up to 3 bounded micro-moves of movable passives (R/C/L/ferrite/diode only - never a hub IC, nor a locked, RF-fenced, (near …)-bound or diff-pair part), re-route ONCE on the moved poses, and keep the trial only when it routes strictly more with no new fab-blocking DRC. Persists nothing: placement_repair.moves[] is shaped for set_part_poses, so an accepted trial is one call away from a saved layout. Default off; with it off the run is byte-identical to one before this existed.

tools.name: route_order_search
tools.description: Search the ROUTING ORDER of a contended net cluster and report the best ordering found, as a paste-ready (pcb-plan (route …)) wave reorder. Wave order IS routing order - earlier waves route first and claim the cleanest space - so which of two nets contending for one corridor goes first can decide whether the other closes at all. Measured on barracuda: moving the v3v3a-pour wave above control-clock-escape (ONE transposition) took a fresh route from 76/90 to 78/90 and its DRC errors from 51 to 32, because closing V_3V3A cascaded into GND, V_5VA, BOOST22_SW and an ADF chip-select. This tool runs those experiments for you. Per call it routes a BASELINE with the authored plan, derives the contended cluster from that route's stuck[] diagnoses (the nets that name each other as blockers, plus the blockers they name - override with nets=[…]), then tries candidate orderings: every ordering when the cluster has <=4 nets, otherwise seeded heuristics (blocker-first, blocked-first, pours-first, signals-first, reverse, single-net promotion/demotion, adjacent transpositions). An ordering re-deals ONLY the priority slots the cluster's own nets already hold, so every other net keeps its authored priority exactly and the winner is expressible as 'reorder these wave forms, leave the rest'. Every trial ranks geometry DRC errors first, then CONNECTIVITY ORACLE completion, then geometry cost. A more connected illegal result cannot outrank a clean one. scope='cluster' (default) re-routes only the cluster's nets on top of the saved layout's copper for everything else - tens of seconds a trial, but it CANNOT show a cascade into out-of-cluster nets, because their copper is held fixed; scope='full' routes the whole board fresh per trial (minutes each) and is the mode whose numbers a ?route=1 describe reproduces. Use cluster to shortlist, full to confirm. RECORDS ITS TRIALS: every trial it runs (baseline included) is appended to the design's trial-memory sidecar (`<design>.trials.json`, the one record_route_trial writes and list_route_trials reads) tagged source='order_search' with the ordering it tried, so the most expensive search in the system leaves a trace instead of making you hand-transcribe it. It edits NO design file - the winning ordering is still guidance you apply. Returns {name, scope (used), scope_requested, scope_note, cluster[] (net names in authored routing order), trials_run, wall_ms, probe_ms (wall spent on the cluster-deriving probe route - 0 when you named the cluster), baseline{routed,total,drc_errors,vias,trace_mm}, trials[] ranked best-first each {rank, trial, label, baseline, order[], routed, total, drc_errors, vias, trace_mm, delta_routed, delta_drc_errors, ms}, suggestion (printable DSL guidance)}.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

nets.description: Explicit cluster to search (array or comma string), instead of deriving one from the baseline route's stuck diagnoses. Order does not matter - the tool sorts them into authored routing order first. Names resolve full or bare-leaf, case-insensitively.

layout.description: Saved layout to search against (default: the starred ★ snapshot).

max_trials.description: Ceiling on trials per call, baseline included (default 12, hard max 48). Each trial is one route: tens of seconds under cluster scope, minutes under full.

scope.description: cluster (default): re-route only the cluster's nets, holding the saved layout's other copper fixed - fast, but blind to cascades into out-of-cluster nets. full: route the whole board fresh per trial - slow, and the mode the wave order was authored for.

record.description: Append this run's trials to the design's trial-memory sidecar (default true). Set false for a throwaway probe you do not want in the log.

tools.name: diagnose_net
tools.description: Inspect ONE named net on the shown saved PCB copper, including pours, arcs and RF paths. Does not reroute or persist. Returns source:'shown_copper', fresh_route:false, and status:'routed' with saved trace_mm/vias/layers, or status:'failed' with failure_mode:'disconnected_copper' and open_nets containing terminal islands and gap endpoints. Gap lines identify disconnected terminals, not proven legal paths. drc_list contains relevant violation IDs, coordinates and both involved parties. Works independently of the whole-board diagnostic cap. Net names resolve full or bare-leaf, case-insensitively.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

net.description: The net to diagnose. Matches a net's full flattened name or its bare leaf (amp1/AMP_IN or AMP_IN), case-insensitively.

layout.description: Diagnose against a specific saved layout instead of the starred ★ one.

sub.description: Scope to a single sub-block (slugified sub-block name).

tools.name: describe_thermal
tools.description: Screening-grade steady-state thermal analysis of a design (or a bare lib/modules module, resolved standalone through its parameter defaults). Lumped and layout-free: one junction temperature per part, Tj = Ta + P*thetaJA, no coupling between parts - the paper check a designer does before committing to a package, answering 'will this part cook in still air, or does the board need airflow / a heatsink'. Each part's dissipation comes from its explicit (power W), else its annotated (i-typ A) pin currents times the resolved rail voltage, else a regulator's back-computed conversion loss; thetaJA comes from the library part's (thermal (theta-ja C-per-W)) or, failing that, a package-name estimate the row flags as estimated. Returns {ambient_c, verdict (passive_ok|needs_airflow|needs_heatsink|over_limit|insufficient_data), limiting_ref, max_ambient/min_ambient {c, ref}, counts {with_power, with_thermal, unknown_power}, parts[] with power/theta/limits/result blocks (unknown figures are null, never 0)}. The same bytes GET /api/thermal/:name returns. Read-only.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

ambient.description: Ambient temperature in degrees Celsius to screen at. Defaults to 25 (bench air).

layout.description: Which SAVED PCB layout to spread the heat over (default: the design's default board - its starred layout, else an auto-placed one). Two saved layouts of one design are two different boards for heat: the same parts, placed differently, over different pours and via stitching, running at different temperatures. A name nobody saved is answered with a sentence saying so rather than the default board's temperatures under the wrong name. List the names with describe_pcb_layout.

tools.name: preview_escape_assignment
tools.description: Preview the JOINT escape assignment for a set of contended nets on a design's blessed PCB placement - read-only, routes nothing. Where several nets leave one connector/QFN through the same channel, the autorouter routes them ONE AT A TIME and the first ones starve the rest; this computes all their lanes at once, the way a hand router would. It finds the nets' shared hub, the direction their destinations lie in, cuts a corridor cross-section at the tightest constriction they all still fit through, slices its free intervals into track-pitch lanes, and maps nets onto lanes so lane order follows endpoint order (no two cross). Returns JSON {name, ok, reason, hub, direction (north|south|east|west), layer, corridor {cut,lo,hi,pitch}, lane_count, lanes[] {pos,x,y}, assignments[] {net,ref,pad,ideal,lane,x,y} (lane null = no lane was left for that net), unknown_nets[], dsl (a pasteable (pcb-plan (route ...)) fragment giving each assigned net its lane as an ordered waypoint)}. To apply the assignment permanently instead, put (assign-escapes) on the wave that selects these nets - it re-solves as parts move.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

nets.description: The contended nets, as an array or a comma-separated string. At least two must exist on the board.

layer.description: Optional copper face to fan the lanes out on (e.g. "F.Cu"). Default: the hub's own side.

hub.description: Optional escape-part ref-des. Default: the part hosting pads of the most named nets.

tools.name: record_route_trial
tools.description: Append one routing experiment's result to a design's trial-memory sidecar (`<design>.trials.json`) - the loop-hygiene half of route_experiment. Pass the numbers you got back from route_experiment (score, routed, total, vias, trace_mm, drc_errors) plus the plan you tried and a note observation; the server RECORDS them, it does NOT re-route to verify. Use this so you (and the next agent) can list-before-the-next-edit and avoid re-proposing a reverted plan / oscillating A->B->A. Ids are monotonic (max+1, never reused after a remove); the log caps at 100 entries (recording the 101st drops the oldest). No timestamps - every write is git-autocommitted with author attribution, so ordering/history come from git. Rows recorded this way are tagged source='agent'; route_order_search writes its own rows tagged source='order_search', so you never need to transcribe a search by hand. Returns {ok:true, id (the new entry's id), count (entries after any cap eviction)}.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

plan.description: The (pcb-plan …) override text that was tried, or a short human label for it.

score.description: The deterministic route_score from route_experiment (may be negative).

trace_mm.description: Total routed copper length in mm.

note.description: Your free-form observation about this trial (optional).

tools.name: list_route_trials
tools.description: Return a design's recorded routing trials (from `<design>.trials.json`), oldest->newest, so you can check 'did I already try this plan?' BEFORE proposing the next DSL edit - the oscillation guard for the constraint-DSL routing loop. Read-only. Each trial is {id, plan, score, routed, total, vias, trace_mm, drc_errors, note, source}. source is 'agent' for a row you recorded by hand and 'order_search' for one route_order_search recorded from its own run (rows written before the field existed read as 'agent', which is what they were). Returns {trials:[…], count}. Spotting an A->B->A oscillation in this history is your job; the server only remembers.

name.description: Design name (basename of src/<name>.sexp), or a lib/modules module name.

tools.name: remove_route_trial
tools.description: Delete one trial from a design's `<design>.trials.json` by id (parity with remove_design_note; for pruning a junk or superseded entry). Remaining ids are left as-is and are never reused. Returns {ok:true}, or an error if no trial has the given id.

id.description: The trial id to remove (as returned by record_route_trial / list_route_trials).

tools.name: set_part_poses
tools.description: Move parts on a design's working (or named) PCB layout and persist the poses into its <design>.layouts.json sidecar. Each pose is {ref, x_mm, y_mm, rot?, side?, locked?}: ref is a component ref-des (C3, buck/U1) or its module-local origin key (resolved exact-ref first, then origin key scoped by sub-block prefix); x_mm/y_mm are the part CENTRE in board mm (y grows DOWN, matching describe_pcb_layout); rot degrees CCW; side top|bottom (bottom mirrors + routes on B.Cu); locked true refuses viewer drag. Unlisted parts keep their poses; a moved part's nets' persisted copper is dropped (stale); an unknown ref fails the whole call without writing. Returns {ok, live_version, layout, total_parts, moved, routes_dropped, updated[]}.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs) or a lib/modules module name.

poses.description: Parts to move: [{ref, x_mm, y_mm, rot?, side?, locked?}, ...].

layout.description: Target a named saved layout (module boards) instead of the working/starred one.

tools.name: set_board_outline
tools.description: Draw the working layout's board outline and persist it into <design>.layouts.json. Supply a rectangle {x,y,w,h} in mm (top-left origin, w/h positive) via rect, OR a closed polygon of >=3 [x,y] mm vertices via pts (its bbox fills the rect fields). The outline becomes the placement's board edge — drawn by every renderer, checked by the board-edge DRC, and profiled as the Gerber Edge.Cuts. Bootstraps a fresh auto placement when the design has no layout yet. Returns {ok, live_version, layout, outline}.

name.description: Design name or a lib/modules module name.

rect.description: Rectangle outline {x,y,w,h} in mm (w/h must be positive).

pts.description: Polygon outline as >=3 [x,y] mm vertex pairs.

layout.description: Target a named saved layout instead of the working/starred one.

tools.name: route_pcb
tools.description: Autoroute the working layout's current poses at the design's resolved routing rules. Route the WHOLE board, or incrementally scope it to a named group / specific nets (route only those, keeping the rest of the board's copper untouched). Naming any scope is incremental by default. An authored (pcb-plan (route ...)) still controls wave order plus preferred/allowed layers underneath. A completed reference_layout can teach the native router its per-net path topology and reserve its proven transition sites; each net is synthesized against that topology first and exact reference copper is retained only as a fallback when synthesis still fails. Post-route topology cleanup removes loose trace stubs and connectivity-redundant non-ground vias before persistence. Returns {ok, live_version, layout, routed, total, unrouted[], drc, drc_errors, drc_warnings, diff_warnings, artifact_warnings, wall_ms, trace_mm, tracks, vias, reference_guided, reference_replayed, pcb_plan, plan_warnings, selected_only, selected, groups, scope} — scope lists the concrete net names routed (or "all"). Reports applied and cancelled. A cancelled candidate never replaces saved copper; top-level connectivity and copper counts describe the retained board, while candidate reports attempted counts and validation_complete:false. Scoped route counts describe the merged board.

name.description: Design name or a lib/modules module name.

groups.description: Route only these net groups — each token resolves (case-insensitively) to a net-class name, then a criticality class (rf, clock, switch_node, feedback, analog, input_rail, power, ground, signal), then a sub-block slug, then a net name. Multiple groups route together. Incremental by default: every other net keeps its copper.

nets.description: Route only these explicit net names (unioned with groups). Incremental by default. Omit both nets and groups to route the whole board.

selected_only.description: Incremental routing. Defaults to true whenever nets/groups is given: route only the scoped nets and retain all other working copper as a physical obstacle. Set false to instead re-route the whole board and merely ADOPT the scoped nets' fresh copper (the legacy scoped-adopt behaviour).

layout.description: Route a named saved layout instead of the working/starred one.

reference_layout.description: Learn per-net path topology and reserve proven transition sites from this completed saved layout. The native router synthesizes against the learned paths and falls back to exact reference copper only for nets it cannot reproduce.

effort.description: Retry tier for this persisted route run. one_shot performs one deterministic native pass before returning a candidate for close_open_nets; standard uses the full escalate, rip-up, and rescue ladder. Absent keeps the design-authored effort.

defer_drc.description: Checkpoint routed copper and return without the expensive full-board DRC report. The response sets drc_deferred true; run run_fab_readiness after the final automatic batch.

tools.name: save_pcb_layout
tools.description: Persist the current working state as a named saved layout, optionally starred (the star default that the KiCad sync + fab outputs read). Every block - designs included - keeps a multi-snapshot history, so naming layout_name forks the working state into a new candidate alongside the others; each is then viewable at /pcb-layout/<name>?layout=<layout>. Returns {ok, live_version, starred, layout}.

name.description: Design name or a lib/modules module name.

layout_name.description: Name for this snapshot. Default: overwrite the working layout in place. Naming a new one forks the working state into a separate candidate, keeping the existing layouts.

star.description: Mark this the starred (default) layout, clearing any other star.

tools.name: clear_routes
tools.description: Drop persisted routed tracks and vias from the working layout — all of them, a net/group scope, or one selected via near an exact coordinate. Keeps poses, board outline, silkscreen text, and user-authored copper zones so power pours remain as input to the next route. The inverse of route_pcb, sharing its scope vocabulary. Returns {ok, live_version, layout, cleared} (segment count removed).

name.description: Design name or a lib/modules module name.

groups.description: Clear only these net groups — same tokens as route_pcb (a net-class, a criticality class like rf/clock, a sub-block slug, or a net name).

nets.description: Only clear these explicit net names' copper (unioned with groups). Omit both to clear all copper. Required with x/y coordinate scoping.

x.description: Optional via-centre X in board mm for surgical clearing; requires y and a nets/groups scope.

y.description: Optional via-centre Y in board mm for surgical clearing; requires x and a nets/groups scope.

radius.description: Match radius in mm around x/y (default 0.05). Coordinate-scoped clearing removes matching vias only.

layout.description: Target a named saved layout instead of the working/starred one.

tools.name: add_tracks
tools.description: Append polyline tracks and optional vias to a saved PCB layout, then check physical connectivity and DRC. Coordinates are board mm (x right, y down); widths and via sizes default to the net class. Copper adding geometry errors is rejected by default. Check applied: top-level added_tracks/added_vias, drc/drc_errors and routed/total/open describe the committed board. A rejected edit reports applied:false, rolled_back:true and zero added objects. candidate contains attempted counts, connectivity and drc_list with exact violation IDs, coordinates and involved parties. Use diagnose_net to inspect the current connection before drawing a legal bridge.

name.description: Design name or a lib/modules module name.

tracks.description: Polylines to draw. Each is one net on one copper layer; consecutive points become track segments. Use a via to change layer mid-route.

net.description: Net name exactly as describe_pcb_layout reports it (sub-block nets keep their prefix, e.g. "adf4159/ADF_CE").

layer.description: Copper layer name, e.g. "F.Cu" or "B.Cu" (inner layers per the design's (stackup ...)).

points.description: At least 2 [x,y] vertices in board mm (y grows DOWN).

width.description: Track width in mm. Omit to use the net's (net-class (width ...)) or the board default.

vias.description: Vias to drop, typically where a track changes layer.

net.description: Net name the via belongs to.

x.description: Via centre X in board mm.

y.description: Via centre Y in board mm (y grows DOWN).

dia.description: Via pad diameter in mm. Omit for the net-class default.

drill.description: Via drill diameter in mm. Omit for the net-class default.

span.description: Optional layer SPAN of the barrel as two copper-layer names, e.g. ["F.Cu","In2.Cu"]. Omit for the full-stack through via every board uses today. The span round-trips through the saved layout; routing, DRC and drill output still treat every via as through, so this is schema groundwork for blind/buried vias, not yet a geometry change. An unknown layer name rejects the whole request.

layout.description: Target a named saved layout instead of the working/starred one.

tools.name: close_open_nets
tools.description: Finish the nets the autorouter gave up on: route the copper that closes a saved layout's remaining airwires, one hop per open copper island, verified against the connectivity oracle. For each open net the tool asks fab_readiness where the islands are, then either STITCHES a plane/pour via beside a stranded pad (how a plane-carried net such as GND rejoins - a surface trace between two QFN ground pads is usually impossible) or MAZES a bridge between the two pads, retrying behind a rip-up of the foreign copper sealing a pad's escape. A hop is KEPT only when the oracle then reports fewer islands on that net AND the ERROR-severity geometry DRC count stays within the accept gate's ceiling - by default the count on the board as it stands (errors may leave, never come back), or the absolute drc_error_budget when the caller declares one; otherwise every byte of it is rolled back, so the call can never make the board worse than the caller said it would accept. A separate differential-quality ratchet also rejects an independent pair leg that would increase uncoupled or skew warnings. Ripped foreign copper is deleted and comes back as its own gap on a later round. Unlike route_pcb (which re-routes the whole board and reports the ROUTER's tally, not connectivity) this only adds the missing metal and leaves finished copper alone. Before persistence it runs the shared topology gate to delete loose stubs and connectivity-redundant non-ground vias. Returns {ok, live_version, layout, hops_tried, hops_kept, pair_quality_rejected, ripped_tracks, tracks, vias, drc, drc_errors, drc_warnings, diff_warnings, artifact_warnings, wall_ms, artifact_tracks_pruned, artifact_vias_pruned, routed, total, open[], failed[], nets_vacated, nets_joint_vacated, vacate_hops_tried, vacate_failed[], vacated[]} - routed/total/open come from the same oracle describe_pcb_layout reports. TWO failure ledgers, and only the first answers "what is still wrong with my board": failed[] is the round loop's record - hops on the nets YOU named, against the board just persisted. vacate_failed[] is the wholesale re-route phase's internal churn on the foreign nets its transactions displaced; those name nets that are neither open nor in your scope, and an entry marked rolled_back:true describes copper that was restored byte-for-byte and is not on the board. vacate_hops_tried counts that phase's hops, which hops_tried (the round loop alone) deliberately does not.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

layout.description: Saved layout name to finish (default: the starred snapshot).

nets.description: Restrict the pass to these open nets (array or comma string). Default: every open net. Use it to finish one subsystem, or to retry a single stubborn net without re-walking the board.

rounds.description: Passes over the open-net list (default 4). Round 0 stitches plane-carried nets and bridges the rest; later rounds bridge everything still open.

vacate.description: Run the wholesale re-route phase after the rounds (default true). It takes the whole nets walling a still-open net's corridor off the board, routes that net first, then puts them back - the only move here that can make an already-closed net take a different shape. It runs in two tiers: SINGLE-SEED (one open net at a time, counted in nets_vacated), then JOINT (counted in nets_joint_vacated) - a cluster of still-open nets that provably contend for the same copper, whose corridors are vacated as ONE union and re-closed together under several routing orders, because N nets fighting over one channel cannot be solved by any sequence of single-seed transactions. Both are all-or-nothing: strictly fewer open nets, no net lost, no rise in geometry errors, else the board is restored byte-for-byte. It is also the slow part, and the source of vacate_failed[]. Set false for a fast, strictly additive pass.

drc_error_budget.description: Absolute ceiling on ERROR-severity geometry DRC violations the pass may leave on the board. Default: none, and the gate then refuses any hop that raises the count at all. Set it to the number of errors you are willing to ship with (read drc_errors first) to let a hop spend real headroom: a bridge that closes a net but costs one clearance error is rejected by the default gate and accepted under a budget that covers it. The budget only ever RELAXES the gate - a hop must still make strict connectivity progress, and the count can never exceed the budget. Measured on barracuda it does not pay: a budget of 7 over a six-error board keeps zero extra hops, a budget of 12 keeps two for +4 errors and still leaves GND open, and a budget handed to a whole pass costs a closed net. Aim it at one named net whose hop you have inspected, not at a general pass.

tools.name: clean_route_topology
tools.description: Remove deletion-invariant stored trace sections, recursively exposed loose stubs, and connectivity-redundant non-ground vias without rerouting. Via deletion is greedy and jointly safe: every pad, trace, remaining via, and identified fill component stays connected exactly as before; unnamed legacy fill contacts are conservatively retained. Trace and via candidates have separate full-board gates, so one rejected phase does not block the other. Supports a read-only dry run and an exact net scope.

name.description: Design or module name.

layout.description: Saved layout to clean (default: the starred snapshot).

dry_run.description: Return the candidate plan and safety verdict without writing (default false).

nets.description: Restrict cleanup to these net names; omit for the whole board.

tools.name: normalize_junctions
tools.description: Explicitly normalize persisted same-net trace/trace and trace/via overlaps into exact centreline joins. The candidate is accepted only when error DRC and routed-net connectivity do not regress. Supports a read-only dry run and an exact net scope.

name.description: Design or module name.

layout.description: Saved layout to normalize (default: the starred snapshot).

dry_run.description: Return the candidate and safety verdict without writing (default false).

nets.description: Restrict normalization to these net names; omit for the whole board.

tools.name: restore_layout_snapshot
tools.description: Restore a design's .layouts.json from its protected layout history. The current sidecar is snapshotted first and the revision is bumped, making the restore undoable and preventing stale editor tabs from overwriting it.

name.description: Design name.

id.description: Snapshot timestamp returned by the layout-history API.

tools.name: repair_land_transit
tools.description: Repair persisted same-net copper that crosses or laps one of its own SMD lands without entering through the pad centre. Safely prunes redundant offending tracks, then re-anchors retained copper through land centres. Every accepted edit must reduce own-land warnings without increasing error-severity DRC or losing connectivity. Returns warning, re-anchored-segment, pruned-track, and connectivity counts plus accepted[] and rejected[] net names.

name.description: Design or module name.

layout.description: Saved layout to repair (default: the starred snapshot).

tools.name: stitch_ground_pads
tools.description: Apply the autorouter's final ground-reference pass to an existing saved layout. For every SMD ground pad governed by (design-rules (ground-via-max MM)), it adds a same-net plane via when no existing via is close enough and a DRC-clean site exists within the authored radius; off a same-net poured face it also adds the short surface stub. The whole edit is rolled back if error-severity DRC rises, the distance audit regresses, or connectivity regresses. Returns before/after ground-reference warnings, added copper counts, and connectivity.

name.description: Design or module name.

layout.description: Saved layout to stitch (default: the starred snapshot).

tools.name: generate_fence
tools.description: Finish a saved RF layout by regenerating its trace-following GND via fences and, on an unfiltered run, filling the rest of the board with a centred 5 mm square GND stitching grid. RF rows wrap the closed guide contour around each routed fenced or max-freq net's whole copper union (tracks, variable-width paths, pads, and via barrels), with pitch from (fence (pitch MM)) or lambda-g/10 and edge gap from (fence (offset MM)) or the resolved clearance plus 0.1 mm. The board grid uses the board's default via geometry after RF sites have first claim. If a nominal grid point is blocked, legal mode searches outward for a DRC-clean point no farther than 1 mm away; if none exists, it records one skipped site. mode=legal is the default and vets every generated via against the exact board outline, keepouts, pads, tracks, vias, pairwise clearances, and drill rules, then applies a final whole-board DRC ratchet so drc_errors equals drc_errors_before. mode=all keeps raw non-coincident generated geometry and only reports DRC. Re-running replaces both RF fence rows and the board grid, while a nets filter regenerates only the named RF rows and leaves the board grid untouched. Returns top-level placed, fence_placed, grid_placed, culled, and replaced counts; nets[] reports each RF contour; grid reports placed, candidates, shifted, culled, pitch_mm, relocate_mm, and skipped-by-reason counts.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

layout.description: Saved layout to fence (default: the starred snapshot). Written back into the same row.

nets.description: Restrict regeneration to these fenced or max-freq RF nets (array or comma string). When present, the board-wide stitching grid is left untouched.

mode.description: How hard each generated site is vetted. "legal" (default) places only sites the board accepts, relocates blocked grid points by at most 1 mm, and holds the run to zero new DRC errors. "all" keeps every non-coincident raw site and reports the resulting DRC without culling. Any other value is rejected.

dry_run.description: Report what would be placed without writing the layout. Default false.

tools.name: placement_sensitivity
tools.description: Which parts are load-bearing? Perturb a placed part's pose by a fraction of a millimetre and measure what it costs the route. For each probed part the tool nudges it +/-delta_mm on each axis (optionally +/-90 degrees) and, per nudge, re-routes ONLY the affected scope - the nets landing on that part plus the nets whose copper threads its neighbourhood - against the rest of the board's copper held pinned as an obstacle. A whole-board route per nudge is minutes and cannot be a probe; a scoped one is seconds. The baseline is a scoped re-route at the ORIGINAL pose, so a net the router merely draws differently on a second look is not reported - only a net whose verdict actually depends on the pose. Flip detection uses the connectivity oracle (the same routed/total describe_pcb_layout reports), never the router's own claim. Routes through the shared plan-lowering seam, so an authored (pcb-plan (route ...)) wave order and layer policy steer the probe exactly as they steer a commit. Read-only: nothing is persisted and the board is never moved. Returns {ok, design, layout, delta_mm, parts[], unknown_refs[], limits} where each part carries its scope, baseline routed/total/drc_errors, a per-perturbation routed/drc_errors/flips[] list with wall time, and a verdict ('stable within +/-0.2 mm' or 'load-bearing: SPI_SCK opens on +x'). A net the nudge FIXES ('... closes on -y') is load-bearing too - it means that net fails to route at the pose currently on the board. LIMIT, stated in the payload too: a scoped probe sees contention inside its scope, so damage flowing through a net contended across the whole board (a supply rail, a bus clock) is under-counted - 'stable' means stable against the neighbours listed in scope.nets, not safe to move. Measured on barracuda's lmx2595 group: at the 0.2 mm default this flags 1 of the 3 parts a full-board re-route was known to break; at 1.0 mm it flags all 3. Raise delta_mm when a probe comes back stable.

name.description: Design name (as from list_designs), or a lib/modules module name.

refs.description: Parts to probe (array or comma string). Each matches like describe_pcb_layout's refs: full ref-des ('lmx2595/R42'), sub-block leaf ('R42'), or stable origin name. Names that match nothing come back in unknown_refs.

layout.description: Probe a named saved layout instead of the starred (default) one.

delta_mm.description: Nudge size in mm (default 0.2 - the size of the edits that cost barracuda seven nets). Clamped to 2 mm; past that a 'perturbation' is a re-placement and every net in scope fails for reasons unrelated to sensitivity.

rotations.description: Also probe +/-90 degree rotations of each part (default false). Doubles-and-a-half the routes per part; worth it for a passive whose pad axis matters.

tools.name: run_fab_readiness
tools.description: Run the complete read-only manufacturing release gate against the exact blessed (starred) or named saved layout. Returns the strict schematic/preflight/BOM/centroid/revision gate, full composed raw DRC evidence and policy, stackup/rule/dependency identities, project-source status, and a revision-locked release token. The HTTP Gerber endpoint requires explicit confirmation of that token (428 if absent/stale), requires an explicit waiver for remaining design findings, and fails non-waivably with 500 when evidence or source identity is incomplete.

name.description: Design name or a lib/modules module name.

layout.description: Check a specific saved layout by name instead of the blessed one.

tools.name: get_version
tools.description: Return the current live version integer for a design. Increments on every successful build.

tools.name: run_checks
tools.description: Run unified assertions, ERC, executable component requirements, verification, and datasheet-review checks on a design or module. profile=authoring (default) reports pending/manual and legacy review gaps as warnings; profile=preflight gates them as errors; profile=release adds the component-class profile obligations (profile_incomplete), a cited-requirement demand on every active part, and evaluator warnings as findings. Returns {filtered,profile,changed_refs,changed_nets,assertion_failures:[...],erc:[...],findings:[...],preflight_ok,finding_errors,finding_warnings}.

variant.description: Assembly variant to evaluate the design in, from the design's (variant "NAME") declarations. Omit for its (default) variant, else the base. Population and value overrides reach ERC through the same dnp/value fields an unconditional (dnp) uses, so an unpopulated part is exempted exactly as a DNP part is.

profile.description: Opt-in strict preflight upgrades pending requirements and incomplete datasheet reviews to errors.

changed_since.description: Snapshot id to diff the current design against; findings are filtered to changed instances/nets.

tools.name: get_language_reference
tools.description: The S-expression design-language reference, auto-generated live from the evaluator's own dispatch tables (identical content to docs/language-forms.md - it can never be stale). Covers every special form, builtin operator, (fmt ...) directive, SI numeric-literal suffix, design-scope form (with arity and allowed scopes), and section-name classifier keyword. Returns Markdown. Pass section to fetch a single '## ' section by title (case-insensitive); omit for the full document. An unknown title errors with the live list of valid section titles. Consult this before authoring or editing .sexp design/module files.

section.description: Optional section title, currently one of: Special forms | Builtin operators | String formatting directives | Numeric literals | Design-scope forms | Section-name classifier keywords. Omit for the whole reference.

tools.name: preview_module
tools.description: Evaluate a lib/modules (defmodule ...) standalone with caller-chosen arguments - module-level schematic design without a host board. Instantiates the module itself in a request-local evaluator, so the ref-des it reports are the ones its source declares (nothing is written to disk), and returns view=summary (default): {ok,module,title,ports,instances,nets,sub_blocks,erc,assertions} - assertions surface the module's (assert / assert-range) design math; or view=scene_graph: the full schematic scene-graph JSON (same shape as get_schematic). A module's boundary (port ...) nets naturally look floating when evaluated in isolation - read ERC with that in mind. On eval failure returns {ok:false,error,diagnostic:{file,line,col,message,source_line}}. Module design loop: read/edit lib/modules/<m>.sexp with the VFS tools, preview here with the args you care about, iterate. For module-level LAYOUT, pass the module name directly as name to get_pcb_layout_image / describe_pcb_layout (they resolve module names via a real instantiation found in a design, else a zero-arg call).

args.description: Raw S-expression argument text for the module call, positional or named - e.g. "220k 47k 1k" or "(rfbt 220k) (rfbb 47k) (rled 1k)". Omit for parameter-less modules.

view.description: summary (default) = compact netlist + ERC + assertions; scene_graph = full schematic JSON.

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Restore a design to a prior snapshot. The current state is itself snapshotted first, so the restore is undoable.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a project file. Path is project-relative (e.g. "src/foo.sexp", "lib/components/cap-0402.sexp"). Text files come back in `content` with `binary:false`; binary files (.pdf, .step, .png, .jpg, .gif, .zip, .gz, .tar, .bin, .kicad_pcb_bin) come back in `base64` with `binary:true`. write_file is text-only, so PDFs and other binary files are read-only via CLI — the user adds them by dropping into lib/datasheets/ on disk or via the browser library page. Optional `offset` and `limit` window the response and are measured in BYTES, not lines; an `offset` at or past EOF returns an error. Always returns the full file's `sha256` so you can pass it as `expected_sha256` on a follow-up write to defend against concurrent edits. Reads are sandboxed: files under auth/, oauth_clients.json, .git/, and similar credentials are denied. See docs/webserver-api.md for the readable/writable path table.

offset.description: Byte offset (NOT a line number) to start reading at (default 0). An offset at or past the end of the file is an error.

limit.description: Max number of BYTES (NOT lines) to return (default = to end of file).

tools.name: list_dir
tools.description: List directory entries under `path` (project-relative; pass empty string for the project root). Each entry has {path, kind: file|dir|symlink|other, size, mtime}. Pass `recursive=true` to walk the subtree. `max_entries` caps the response (default 1024). Denied entries (auth/, oauth state) are silently filtered. Note: bare `lib` is not directly listable — use list_library or list_dir on a subdir like `lib/components/`.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files matching a glob pattern. Supports `*` (any chars in segment), `?` (one char), and `**` (any depth). Optional `base` restricts the search to a subdirectory. Output paths are project-relative.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Atomically write `content` (text — UTF-8 passes through verbatim, including µ/°/± and other non-ASCII inside quoted strings) to a sandboxed path (writes go to a tmp file then rename, so a crash never leaves a half-written file). Writes are restricted to src/, lib/components/, lib/modules/, lib/pinouts/, lib/footprints/, lib/sources/, and blocks/. lib/datasheets/ is read-only via CLI — PDFs are added by hand on disk or via the browser library page. Refuses to write through symlinks or to .layout files (binary, regenerated by build). Optional `append:true` concatenates `content` onto the existing file (empty if it doesn't exist yet) instead of replacing it. Optional `expected_sha256` enables CAS — pass the sha256 from a prior read to fail loudly if the file changed underneath you (for an append the CAS is checked against the PRE-append file). The response always carries the new full-file sha256. Returns `dirty_designs` (designs whose import graph reaches the file) and `library_changes` (which library entity, if any, the write touched — populated even when no design imports the file yet).

expected_sha256.description: Optional CAS guard: write fails if the file's current sha256 differs

append.description: When true, concatenate content onto the existing file instead of replacing it (default false).

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Find `old_string` once in the file and replace it with `new_string`. Fails with `old_string not found` on zero matches and `ambiguous match` on multiple matches (unless `replace_all=true`). Same sandbox rules as write_file. Optional `expected_sha256` for CAS.

old_string.description: Exact text to find. Include enough surrounding context to make it unique.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of failing on multi-match (default false)

tools.name: delete_file
tools.description: Delete a single file under the write sandbox. Refuses to delete directories or symlinks. Returns dirty_designs.

tools.name: move_file
tools.description: Rename `from` → `to`. Both paths are sandbox-checked under the write allowlist. Atomic on the same filesystem.

tools.name: build
tools.description: Re-evaluate `<name>.sexp`, resolve the BOM, run unified ERC/requirement/datasheet-review validation, render, and bump the live version. Returns {ok,version,eval_ok,profile,snapshot,error?,assertion_failures[],erc[],findings[],preflight_ok,finding_errors,finding_warnings,warnings[],module_dependencies[{source,module,source_sha256}]}. The dependency digests identify the exact reusable module sources used by this build so review/CI can detect library drift. profile=authoring (default) is backward-compatible; profile=preflight refuses to publish a new live version when ERC or strict preflight errors remain.

name.description: Design name (basename of src/<name>.sexp)

severity.description: Optional: filter returned erc[] and findings[] to this severity.

profile.description: Opt-in strict validation gate before publishing the live build.

tools.name: regenerate_pinout
tools.description: Re-run the KiCad → netlisp pinout converter (same code path as `netlisp convert-pinout` CLI). Reads `<source>` (must be under lib/sources/, e.g. "lib/sources/adar2004accz.kicad_sym"), generates the auto-generated pinout content, and writes it to lib/pinouts/<name>.sexp. The pinout's `;; source: …` header records the linkage so describe_component can later surface `pinout_source` for the next agent. If the upstream pin name is wrong (e.g. the datasheet says RFIN4+ but the .kicad_sym says REFIN4+, or pin 40 is named VPOS instead of VPOS5), edit the .kicad_sym in lib/sources/ first — that path is writable — then call this to regenerate. Output `name` defaults to the source basename minus .kicad_sym; pass `filter` for multi-symbol library files. Returns {ok:true, source, path, bytes_written, sha256, dirty_designs, library_changes} or {ok:false, error}.

source.description: Path to the .kicad_sym source file under lib/sources/

name.description: Optional output basename (defaults to source basename without .kicad_sym extension)

filter.description: Optional symbol-name filter for multi-symbol library files

tools.name: parse_kicad_netlist
tools.description: Parse a KiCad board (.kicad_pcb) into a netlist PREVIEW without importing anything — the read-only front half of import_kicad. Reads the board file directly off disk (board_path may be ABSOLUTE, e.g. a NAS mount — same trust model as a design's (kicad-pcb ...) sync path) and returns its footprints as a classified netlist. Returns {ok:true, part_count, net_count, components:[{ref, value, lib, family, dnp, pads:[{pad, function, net}]}]}: family is the existing passive component-family the part maps onto (e.g. "cap-0402") or null for a custom part; net_count counts the DISTINCT connected nets; each pad's net is "" when the pad is unconnected (an empty net or a KiCad unconnected-* stub). Writes nothing. Returns {ok:false, error} when board_path does not end in .kicad_pcb, the file cannot be read, or it is not a valid KiCad board.

board_path.description: Path to the .kicad_pcb file. May be absolute (e.g. a NAS mount).

tools.name: inspect_kicad_layout
tools.description: Read a KiCad .kicad_pcb as a normalized PHYSICAL layout snapshot without writing it: fixed footprint poses/pads, nets, copper segments/arcs/vias, Edge.Cuts bounds, zones/keepouts, layer utilization, width distribution, total routed length, and routing-relevant rules/net classes/patterns from the adjacent same-stem .kicad_pro. Returns compact deterministic JSON for scoring or reference-board experiments. Set include_nets=true for per-net pad/segment/arc/via/zone/length metrics.

board_path.description: Absolute or project-relative path to the .kicad_pcb file.

include_nets.description: Include per-net physical routing metrics (default false).

tools.name: benchmark_kicad_routing
tools.description: Create a non-destructive routing benchmark from a completed KiCad board. With only reference_path, virtually erase all traces/arcs/vias (or only nets[]) and report the untouched seed/removed copper metrics; no file is written. Add candidate_path to score a separately generated .kicad_pcb against fixed footprint poses, outline, completeness, adjacent reference-project hard rules, via count, and length. Lower objective is better; geometry drift and missing nets dominate.

candidate_path.description: Optional separately generated candidate .kicad_pcb to score.

nets.description: Optional net subset for leave-one-net/pair/section experiments; omit to erase/score all nets.

tools.name: export_kicad_sch
tools.description: Export the design's KiCad SCHEMATIC — the .kicad_sch sheet hierarchy (root + one child sheet per (section ...) / (sub-block ...) module) plus the project sidecars that make its library references resolve in KiCad: sym-lib-table, fp-lib-table, <name>.kicad_pro, and netlisp.kicad_sym. Ref-des and net names are the SAME flattening the netlist exporter uses, and each symbol carries the instance UUID the netlist and the board already carry. Every sheet is re-parsed and structurally self-checked before it is returned. WITHOUT output_dir this is read-only and returns a summary — {ok,name,sheets,components,vendor_bodies,instances,bytes_total,files[{name,bytes}],sidecars[{name,bytes}],written:false} — never the sheet text, which runs to megabytes on a real board; fetch the bytes from GET /api/kicad-sch/<name> (a store-only zip) when you need them. WITH output_dir the files are written there under their bare names (they must stay in ONE directory — the root's Sheetfile links name bare siblings); an existing sidecar is kept, never overwritten. output_dir must be ABSOLUTE, free of '..', and OUTSIDE the project directory: this is an export, not a design edit, and a write into the project would be auto-committed to the design repo as if you had authored it. Footprint links resolve only when footprints.pretty/ (from export-kicad) sits beside the sheets, so a schematic-only export still reports KiCad footprint_link_issues warnings.

name.description: Design name or a lib/modules module name.

output_dir.description: Absolute directory to write the sheets + sidecars into. Must be outside the project directory. Omit for a read-only summary.

vendor.description: Draw parts from their original lib/sources/*.kicad_sym when one exists (default true). false forces a synthesised box for every part — the --no-vendor-symbols twin.

flat.description: Force one flat sheet regardless of size (default false). A real board then comes out roughly a metre square on a single page; prefer the hierarchy.

tools.name: sync_kicad_sch
tools.description: Push the design's KiCad SCHEMATIC into the LIVE KiCad project directory the design's (kicad-pcb "<path>") form names — the schematic counterpart of the board sync. The sheets are named after the KiCad PROJECT, not the netlisp design ('Cyclops Digital.kicad_pcb' gives 'Cyclops Digital.kicad_sch' plus 'Cyclops Digital-<section>.kicad_sch' children and a matching .kicad_pro), so KiCad opens them as THE project schematic and a second netlisp design pushed into the same folder cannot collide. GUARDED: an existing sheet is replaced only when it is a previous netlisp push ((generator "netlisp")) or an empty eeschema stub (a (kicad_sch ...) with no placed symbol, sheet, wire, label or graphic); anything else REFUSES THE WHOLE PUSH by name and writes nothing, unless force is set. A KiCad lock file (~<file>.lck) anywhere in the project directory refuses even with force — close KiCad instead. Sidecars: an absent .kicad_pro or sym-lib-table is created, an existing one is never touched (a sym-lib-table with no netlisp row is reported with the exact line to add), the fp-lib-table belongs to the board sync and is left alone, and netlisp.kicad_sym is regenerated. Replaced files roll into backups/<name>.bak-<stamp> beside the board, newest 10 kept. Everything is validated before anything is written and each file is staged under a temp name then renamed, so a failure cannot leave a torn set of sheets. Returns {ok,name,dir,project,root,dry_run,written,summary{create,overwrite,keep,advise,skip,refuse},refusal?,files[{name,action,bytes,note}]}; a refusal comes back as ok:false with the reason, not as an error.
