CAVEAT: KiCad escapes '/' in net names and netlisp labels each per-pin bypass stub as its rail, so these sheets must NOT drive "Update PCB from Schematic" on a netlisp-synced board — netlisp's own netlist and the file-based board sync stay the board authority.

name.description: Design name. The design must declare a (kicad-pcb "<path>") form; without one there is no project directory to push into and the call is refused by name.

dry_run.description: Report the per-file plan without writing anything (default false).

force.description: Replace a sheet that is neither a previous netlisp push nor an empty eeschema stub (default false). Does NOT override a KiCad lock on the project.

tools.name: import_kicad
tools.description: Import an existing KiCad board (.kicad_pcb) INTO this netlisp project — the CLI twin of the `netlisp import-kicad` CLI. Reads the board file directly off disk (board_path may be ABSOLUTE, e.g. a NAS mount), maps standard passives onto existing component families, and WRITES generated library files under lib/{components,pinouts,footprints} for every other part plus the design source src/<name>.sexp (existing library files are never overwritten). This is a MUTATION: after a successful import the new design still needs a `build` to evaluate and render it. Pass dry_run:true to report the counts WITHOUT writing any files. fold_channels folds repeated per-channel structure (CH1_*/CH2_*/… net families) into a generated defmodule + per-channel sub-blocks; fold_prefix overrides channel detection and implies fold_channels. Returns {ok:true, parts, family_mapped, custom_parts, lib_written, lib_existing, nets, dropped_pins, design_path, fold:{module, channels, parts_each, skipped}?, dry_run} (fold present only when channel folding fired), or {ok:false, error} when board_path does not end in .kicad_pcb, the file is missing/unreadable, or it is not a valid KiCad board.

board_path.description: Path to the .kicad_pcb file. May be absolute (e.g. a NAS mount).

name.description: Design name → written to src/<name>.sexp.

title.description: Human-readable design-block title (default: the board filename without its extension).

dry_run.description: Report counts without writing any lib/ or src/ files (default false).

fold_channels.description: Fold repeated per-channel structure into a generated module + sub-blocks (default false).

tools.name: list_design_notes
tools.description: Return the per-design TODO list parsed from `<design>.notes.md`. Each task has an `id` (8-char hex, stable across renames), `text`, `created` (YYYY-MM-DD UTC), and `completed` (YYYY-MM-DD UTC when done, else null). `scratchpad` is any free-form text in the file that isn't a structured task line. Returns {tasks:[{id,text,created,completed}], scratchpad}.

name.description: Design name (basename of src/<name>.sexp)

tools.name: add_design_note
tools.description: Append a new open TODO to a design's `<design>.notes.md`. The note is stamped with today's UTC date and gets a fresh 8-char hex id. Use this to log ERC errors, follow-ups, or pin-mapping fixes that should be addressed in the next revision (e.g. "screen LED pins defined backwards, swap PE5 and PE6"). Pair with `complete_design_note` once the design has been updated. Returns {ok:true, task:{id,text,created,completed:null}}.

name.description: Design name

tools.name: complete_design_note
tools.description: Mark a TODO as done by stamping today's UTC date into its `completed` field. Idempotent: if the task is already done, the existing completion date is preserved. Returns {ok:true} or an error if no task has the given id.

tools.name: reopen_design_note
tools.description: Clear a TODO's completion date so it moves back to the open list. Useful when a fix turns out to be incomplete and the same task needs another revision. Returns {ok:true} or an error if no task has the given id.

tools.name: remove_design_note
tools.description: Delete a TODO from `<design>.notes.md`. The scratchpad section is left intact. Returns {ok:true} or an error if no task has the given id.

tools.name: list_component_requirements
tools.description: List the (requirement ...) design rules declared on a library component (lib/components/<name>.sexp). These are datasheet-derived rules attached to the part itself, so every design that instantiates the part inherits them — they are NOT per-design (for per-design follow-ups use add_design_note). Returns {ok:true, name, requirements:[{id, text, ref:{pdf,page,quote}|null, check_kind}]}. id is the requirement's stable identifier (an explicit (id ...) sub-form if present, else the Crc32 of the text) — pass it to remove_component_requirement or cite it in a (verifies (req "REF" id)) design sign-off. check_kind is the machine-check primitive (decoupling, voltage-range, connected, pullup-range, ...) or null for reviewer-judged rules. Returns {ok:false,error} if the component is missing.

name.description: Component basename, e.g. "stm32n657l0h3q". Same names list_library returns under "components".

tools.name: add_component_requirement
tools.description: Append a (requirement ...) form to a library component's lib/components/<name>.sexp. Records a datasheet-derived design rule ON THE PART (e.g. a pin that must be tied to a rail, a mandatory decoupling cap, an absolute-max voltage) so every design that uses the part inherits it and the build-time review can enforce it. WHAT QUALIFIES AS A REQUIREMENT: a rule a schematic can VIOLATE and a reviewer or check can flag — a supply rail outside its valid range, a missing mandatory pull-up or decoupling cap, a pin that must be tied to a specific net, an absolute-maximum that must not be exceeded. WHAT DOES NOT: capabilities and feature descriptions ('Fast-mode I2C up to 1 MHz', 'Schmitt-trigger inputs', 'bidirectional level translation'), typical or informational specs ('standby current 2µA typ', 'operating temperature -40..85C'), power-on or behavioral notes ('I/Os are high-Z at reset'), and restatements or duplicates of another requirement. None of those can be 'violated' by a wiring choice, so they are NOT requirements — if you want to record them, use add_design_note on the design instead. Litmus test before adding: 'could a schematic break this rule, and would the review catch the break?' If no, do not add it. Keep one rule per requirement (don't bundle two constraints into one line); datasheet scrapes tend to over-collect, so prune aggressively. The requirement gets a stable id derived from its text (Crc32), matching the id used by (verifies ...) sign-offs. Optionally cite the datasheet via ref_pdf/ref_page/ref_quote. Optionally attach a machine check by passing a complete (check ...) S-expression in `check`; it is validated by the same parser the build uses and rejected if unrecognized. Existing source formatting and comments are preserved. Returns {ok:true,id,text}; returns {ok:false,error} on a duplicate (same derived id), an unknown/malformed check, or a missing component. To edit a requirement, remove it and add the new text (the id is text-derived).

name.description: Component basename, e.g. "stm32n657l0h3q"

text.description: The requirement statement (prose). The stable id is derived from this text.

ref_pdf.description: Optional datasheet filename to cite, e.g. "an5967.pdf" (should already be under lib/datasheets/).

ref_quote.description: Optional verbatim datasheet snippet supporting the requirement.

check.description: Optional machine check as a complete S-expression, e.g. (check (connected (pin "PDR_ON") (pin "VDDA18_AON"))). Validated before writing. See a requirement's check_kind in describe_component / list_component_requirements for the available primitives.

tools.name: remove_component_requirement
tools.description: Delete a (requirement ...) form from a library component's lib/components/<name>.sexp, matched by its id (from list_component_requirements / describe_component) or by exact text. Removes the whole form and the line it sits on; if it was the last requirement, the component's closing paren is preserved. Other source formatting and comments are untouched. Supply either id (preferred) or text. Returns {ok:true,removed_id}; returns {ok:false,error} if nothing matches.

name.description: Component basename

id.description: Requirement id to remove (preferred). Get it from list_component_requirements.

text.description: Exact requirement text to remove, as an alternative to id.

tools.name: read_datasheet
tools.description: Extract a window of text from a datasheet PDF under lib/datasheets/. Returns {ok:true,name,sha256,total_bytes,offset,returned_bytes,truncated,content}; sha256 is the current PDF identity to record in `(datasheet-review ...)`. Extraction is bounded and cached; page through long files with offset/limit.

name.description: Datasheet filename (e.g. "lm66100.pdf" or "lm66100")

offset.description: Byte offset into the extracted text to start at (default 0)

limit.description: Max bytes of text to return (default 20000)

tools.name: download_footprint
tools.description: Fetch a part's ECAD model from Component Search Engine (componentsearchengine.com) by part number and import it into the project library in one step. Searches the site, scrapes the SamacSys part id, downloads the model ZIP, then runs it through the same converter as the /library zip upload: writes lib/components/<name>.sexp (linking pinout + footprint + manufacturer/MPN), lib/pinouts/<name>.sexp, lib/footprints/<name>.sexp, and lib/models/<name>.step (when a 3D model is present), plus the raw KiCad sources under lib/sources/. Authentication: the model download uses HTTP Basic auth, so the environment must provide CSE_EMAIL + CSE_PASSWORD (via .env or the environment; read from the environment rather than command arguments); if they are unset the call returns {ok:false}. After a successful import you can reference the new component by its returned `component` name in a design and `build` it. Returns {ok:true, part_name, manufacturer, samac_id, zip, zip_size, component, footprint, pinout, has_3d_model} on success, or {ok:false, stage:"download"|"import", error} on failure (e.g. part not found, rejected credentials, or a zip missing KiCad files).

part_number.description: Manufacturer part number to search for, e.g. "LMX2595RHAT" or "INA228AIDGSR".

manufacturer.description: Optional manufacturer name to disambiguate when multiple parts share a number, e.g. "Texas Instruments". Case-insensitive substring match.

tools.name: download_datasheet
tools.description: Fetch a part's datasheet PDF by part number and store it under lib/datasheets/, where read_datasheet can then extract its text. Tries two sources in order: (1) Component Search Engine (componentsearchengine.com) — tolerates non-exact matches by retrying relaxed variants, scrapes the datasheet link off the part page, downloads + validates the %PDF header; (2) DigiKey as a fallback when CSE has no datasheet on file — resolves the part via the DigiKey Product Information API, unwraps any manufacturer interstitial on its datasheet_url (e.g. TI's gotoUrl redirect), follows redirects, and validates %PDF. Authentication: source 1 needs none (the suggestion API + off-site PDF are public); source 2 needs DIGIKEY_CLIENT_ID + DIGIKEY_CLIENT_SECRET, read server-side, never over CLI. Returns {ok:true, source:"componentsearchengine"|"digikey", file, size, part, manufacturer, datasheet_url} on success. When BOTH sources fail, returns {ok:false, error, cse_error, digikey_error} naming why each one did.

part_number.description: Manufacturer part number to search for, e.g. "LM66100DCKR" or "INA228AIDGSR".

manufacturer.description: Optional manufacturer name to disambiguate when multiple parts share a number, e.g. "Texas Instruments". Case-insensitive substring match.

tools.name: fetch_datasheet
tools.description: Download a datasheet PDF from an explicit URL into lib/datasheets/, where read_datasheet can extract its text and attach_datasheet can declare it on a component. This is the escape hatch for parts the catalogue providers behind download_datasheet do not carry: find the manufacturer's own PDF link, pass it here. For vendor endpoints that require navigation from a product page, pass source_page and it is sent as the validated HTTP Referer. Guarantees: the body is content-sniffed for the %PDF magic (a login wall or cookie interstitial answering 200 is rejected whatever its Content-Type); the target filename is sanitized to lib/datasheets/<name>.pdf and can never escape that directory; the download is capped at 64 MiB and 90 s; an existing file with the SAME bytes is a no-op (status "unchanged", same sha256), and an existing file with DIFFERENT bytes is refused unless you pass overwrite:true, because every (datasheet-review ...) record cites the sha256 a silent replacement would invalidate. Returns {ok:true,name,sha256,bytes,status:"written"|"unchanged"} - record that sha256 in the review. On a name clash: {ok:false,error,name,existing_sha256,sha256}. Writes ONLY into lib/datasheets/, never a design source.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the PDF, e.g. "https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm66100.pdf". Redirects are followed.

name.description: Target filename under lib/datasheets/ (".pdf" is appended if missing). Defaults to the URL's last path segment with any query/fragment dropped. Prefer the manufacturer part number, e.g. "LM66100DCKR.pdf".

source_page.description: Optional absolute manufacturer product-page URL sent as the HTTP Referer when a direct download endpoint otherwise rejects the PDF request.

overwrite.description: Replace a stored file of the same name whose bytes differ. Default false - the fetch is refused instead, so an existing datasheet-review digest cannot be invalidated by accident.

tools.name: attach_datasheet
tools.description: Declare a datasheet on a library component: splices (datasheet "file.pdf") into lib/components/<component>.sexp. This is the LINK step - fetch_datasheet / download_datasheet only put bytes in lib/datasheets/, while this form is what fills an instance's docs.datasheets, what describe_component reports under "datasheets", what a (datasheet-review ...) record must name, and what the datasheet coverage check requires of every active IC. `file` is either a filename already present in lib/datasheets/ (verified to exist) or an absolute http(s) URL for a part whose PDF is not redistributable. Idempotent: a stem already linked (ignoring a re-download counter like "foo (1).pdf") returns {ok:true,status:"already_linked"} without editing. Returns {ok:true,status:"linked",component,file,live_version} on a write.

component.description: Library component name - the lib/components/<component>.sexp basename, e.g. "lm66100".

file.description: A PDF filename in lib/datasheets/ (e.g. "LM66100DCKR.pdf") or an absolute http(s) URL.

tools.name: search_components
tools.description: Search Component Search Engine (componentsearchengine.com) for parts by name/number and return candidate matches WITHOUT importing anything — the read-only counterpart to download_footprint/download_datasheet. The exact query is tried first; if it returns nothing, relaxed variants are tried, so partial or family numbers still match. Each result reports whether CSE has an ECAD model (has_model) and a datasheet (has_datasheet) on file. Typical flow: search_components to find the exact part_number + manufacturer, then call download_footprint (and/or download_datasheet) with that part_number to import it into the library. Authentication: none — the suggestion API is public, so this works with no CSE credentials configured. Returns {ok:true, query, count, results:[{part_number, manufacturer, has_model, has_datasheet}]} or {ok:false, error} (e.g. a network/Cloudflare failure). An empty results array with ok:true means CSE matched nothing.

query.description: Part number or search term, e.g. "INA228" or "W25Q128".

limit.description: Max results to return (default 10, capped at 50).

tools.name: resolve_mpn
tools.description: Resolve a fuzzy query — a vague description or a partial/orderable part number — to real MANUFACTURER part numbers via the DigiKey Product Information API v4, WITHOUT importing anything. This is the discovery step in front of Component Search Engine: DigiKey is good at 'description -> canonical MPN', then you feed a returned mpn to search_components / download_footprint / download_datasheet (which match on an MPN you already know), or to check_stock for the full per-packaging price ladder. Each result also carries a manufacturer DATASHEET URL (a second datasheet source besides CSE), the DigiKey product page URL, the DigiKey orderable part number, plus live stock (quantity_available), the single-unit price (unit_price), and lifecycle status (product_status: Active / Obsolete / Last Time Buy / …) — so a candidate's availability is visible without a second call. Authentication: the environment must provide DIGIKEY_CLIENT_ID and DIGIKEY_CLIENT_SECRET (via .env or the environment; an OAuth2 client-credentials app registered at developer.digikey.com); optionally DIGIKEY_API_BASE to target the sandbox host. Credentials are read server-side and never passed over CLI. DigiKey's KeywordSearch is a keyword AND-match (NOT semantic), so query with terse parametric fragments like the DigiKey search box — value + package + function in a few keywords ("3.3V LDO 1A SOT-223", "current monitor i2c") — not full sentences. If a query returns nothing, the tool auto-relaxes by dropping trailing keywords one at a time and takes the first variant with hits, so over-specific queries degrade gracefully instead of returning empty. Returns {ok:true, query, count, results:[{mpn, manufacturer, description, datasheet_url, product_url, digikey_part_number, quantity_available, unit_price, product_status}]} (datasheet_url/product_url/digikey_part_number/unit_price/product_status may be null; quantity_available is 0 when out of stock) or {ok:false, error} (credentials unset, token rejected, or network failure). An empty results array with ok:true means DigiKey matched nothing even after relaxation.

query.description: Part number, or terse keyword fragments (value + package + function), e.g. "INA228" or "3.3V LDO 1A SOT-223". Avoid full sentences — keyword match, not semantic.

limit.description: Max results to return (default 10, capped at 50).

tools.name: check_stock
tools.description: Live DigiKey stock + pricing for a known manufacturer part number or orderable DigiKey number. The 'is it actually on the shelf, and what does qty-N cost' step after resolve_mpn hands you a candidate MPN. Resolves the query through the same DigiKey Product Information API v4 keyword search as resolve_mpn (so a partial/fuzzy number still matches, auto-relaxing trailing keywords), then returns the FULL per-packaging detail each match omits in resolve_mpn: every orderable packaging variation (Cut Tape, Tape & Reel, Tube, …) with its own live quantity_available, minimum_order_quantity, and the complete quantity price-break ladder (break_quantity / unit_price / total_price). Use this to confirm a part is genuinely stocked and to read real volume pricing — not just a 1-off price. Authentication is identical to resolve_mpn: the environment must provide DIGIKEY_CLIENT_ID and DIGIKEY_CLIENT_SECRET (via .env or the environment; an OAuth2 client-credentials app from developer.digikey.com), optionally DIGIKEY_API_BASE for the sandbox host; credentials are read from the environment rather than command arguments. Prices are in the catalog currency DigiKey returns for the account's locale. Returns {ok:true, query, count, results:[{mpn, manufacturer, description, product_status, quantity_available, unit_price, product_url, digikey_part_number, variations:[{digikey_part_number, package_type, quantity_available, minimum_order_quantity, price_breaks:[{break_quantity, unit_price, total_price}]}]}]} or {ok:false, error}. quantity_available is 0 when out of stock; an empty variations or price_breaks array means DigiKey published none (e.g. a marketplace listing). An empty results array with ok:true means nothing matched even after relaxation.

query.description: Manufacturer part number or DigiKey orderable number, e.g. "INA228AIDGSR" or "296-INA228-ND". A partial number works (keyword match) but an exact MPN gives the cleanest single match.

limit.description: Max matching products to return (default 5, capped at 50). Each result carries full price ladders, so keep this small.

tools.name: optimize_connector_pinout
tools.description: Search connector pin-to-net assignments against the shown PCB placement without editing the schematic or layout. Preserves the connector's existing net-token multiplicities (including repeated power/GND contacts), honours fixed pins, allowed-pin sets, movable-pin sets, adjacent ordered groups, and geometry-derived guard shells. The default is a fast geometric constrained multistart search only: route_trials default is 0, so no autorouter runs. Set route_trials to 1-4 to route-check only that many top candidates in memory with a bounded plan-neutral one-shot route; no candidate is ever persisted. Returns {name,layout,ref,method,optimality,evaluated,feasible,route_trials,candidates[]}, each candidate carrying rank, geometric_cost, full pinout, changes from current, and optional route {routed,total,vias,trace_mm,drc_errors,score}. optimality is explicitly best_found_not_proven because detailed PCB routing is combinatorial.

name.description: Design name or lib/modules module name.

ref.description: Exact connector reference designator, for example J1.

layout.description: Saved layout to optimize against instead of the blessed layout.

fixed.description: Hard pin-to-net map, for example {"15":"IF1_DSA"}. Repeated-net counts cannot exceed the connector's existing count.

movable_pins.description: When present, only these connector pins may change; all others retain their current nets.

groups.description: Adjacent/ordered sensitive groups and optional guard shells.

ignore_nets.description: Nets omitted from geometric cost. With this absent, GND is ignored automatically.

route_trials.description: How many leading candidates to route-check; default is 0, which runs no router.

route_seconds.description: Per-candidate route ceiling when route_trials is nonzero (default 15 seconds).

tools.name: rewrite-pins-by-name
tools.description: Rewrite a design or module source's numeric/string PAD tokens into the pinout FUNCTION NAME the evaluator already resolves them through, so strap and no-connect sign-offs read for themselves: (pin 5 "GND") ;; ILIM plus (strap-ok 5 "ILIM->GND ...") becomes (pin ILIM "GND") plus (strap-ok ILIM ...). Covers (pin PAD... "NET") including multi-pad shorthand and (part ...) bodies, (strap-ok PAD ...), (nc-ok PAD ...), (near "REF" PAD [(own PAD)]) and (decouples "REF" PAD) - the last two resolving through the TARGET ref's pinout. Text is spliced at AST byte spans, so every comment, blank line and column of alignment outside the replaced token survives byte for byte. A pad is rewritten ONLY when the evaluator's own resolver, re-run on the proposed spelling, returns the very pad the original bound to, the function name is unique in the pinout, and the name re-tokenizes to itself; pads with no function name, positional connector pads (function == pad id), repeated function names and parts with no lib/pinouts file are left alone and reported. SAFETY: the ORIGINAL and REWRITTEN sources are both evaluated and flattened, and the write is refused unless their netlists AND their resolved (decouples ...)/(near ...)/(strap-ok ...)/(nc-ok ...) bindings match exactly; a file that does not parse or does not evaluate is refused outright. Default write:false returns the unified diff without touching the file. Returns {ok,file,rewritten,written,netlist_equivalent,parts_without_pinout,positional_parts,skipped[{ref,pad,reason}],skipped_omitted,diff}.

file.description: Project-relative .sexp source to rewrite: a module ("lib/modules/adp7118-ldo.sexp") or a design ("src/boards/barracuda/barracuda.sexp"). Nothing outside lib/modules/ and src/ is accepted.

write.description: Apply the rewrite. Default false: compute it, prove it, and return the diff without touching the file.

refs.description: Optional ref-des allowlist, e.g. ["U1"]. Omit (or pass an empty array) to consider every instance in the file.
